Listen to this article Share The Abia State Government has dissolved the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club , Aba, with immediate effect following the club’s disappointing performance in the ongoing 2026/2027 Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) season. Advertisement Advertisement The decision, announced on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, is part of a wider restructuring exercise aimed at addressing what the government described as administrative, technical and operational challenges affecting the two-time African champions. The announcement was contained in a statement signed by Prince Okey Kanu, the state’s Commissioner for Information, who said the government had reviewed the club’s situation and concluded that far-reaching interventions were necessary to restore its competitive identity. Former Super Eagles captain Kanu Nwankwo, who has served as the club’s chairman since 2023, is among those affected by the management shake-up. “The decision underscores the government’s resolve to undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the two-time CAF Champions League winners, restore the club’s competitive identity and reposition it for sustainable success in Nigerian and continental football,” Kanu said. He added that the government’s review had identified underlying issues affecting the club’s performance, administration and overall operations. Advertisement Enyimba languish in relegation zone The management shake-up comes as the nine-time Nigerian champions continue to struggle in the NPFL. Enyimba are reportedly 18th on the league table, with 11 points from 13 matches and just three victories, leaving the Aba-based club in the relegation zone. The club recent run has raised concerns about the club’s ability to recover and retain its place in the top flight, prompting the state government to move for a comprehensive overhaul of its leadership and football operations.
